chapter_title: Concerning the Purification of these Four Elements
spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation


**
¶2:**
 The four fundamental
 fac
ulties of the spirit
 — love, wisdom, perception, and
 truth — are
 what
 must
 be purified. From their
 origin
 they are holy, living, and illumin
ating,
 for
 they were created
 as
 vessels of the Divine. But when they
 entered into
 the prim
ordial conflict
 between
 good
 and evil, the
 resid
ue of self
-derived
 will
 was min
gled with them, and the fals
ity proce
eding from hell was com
mingled with their
 substance
. And
 when these faculties descended into the natural
 man, they cast off their corrupted
 external truths and deposited them in
 the prop
rium.
 These corruptions, once
 separated out
, become exposed and become a source of
 spiritual destruction
 to the natural man.

**
¶3:** The corruption
 that
 perv
erted
 love dis
gor
ges and
 deposits into
 the natural man is the vital force of
 self
-love
.
 From this vital
 force of
 self
-love arises wrath.
 From wrath arise the
 disordered affections that perv
ade
 the whole natural mind.

**
¶4:** The corru
ptions
 that fals
ified
 truth dischar
ges from
 itself
 are concupiscence.
 From concupiscence ar
ises 
anguish of
 spirit.
 From anguish of
 spirit arises the
 burning
 inflammation
 of ung
over
ned
 desire.

**¶5:**
 The corruption that obsc
ured
 wisdom disgor
ges is
 the proprium itself
 —
 the sense
 that
 one lives
 from
 one
self. From the proprium arises
 darkness
 of understanding. From darkness of understanding ar
ises obst
inate
 hard
ness of will against all
 truth.

**¶6:**
 The corruptions that perv
erted perception disgorges
 are the
 persu
asions of self-condemnation
 and spiritual exposure — thoughts
 that
 proceed
 from the awareness
 of one's own nak
edness before
 the Divine. What
 issues
 from these
 persu
asions is [
*
the text
 breaks
 off;
 likely the
 deep
est in
version
 of perception
:
 spiritual
 desp
air or
 complete
 a
version from self
-knowledge
*].

**¶7:**
 The grief
 that issues
 from all
 of
 these together
 is the summ
ation of these twelve spiritual
 corruptions —
 the full
 cascade by
 which the original
 faculties,
 once
 holy
, produce
 in
 the fallen
 natural man their
 complete
 per
version:
 from
 love into
 w
rath into
 disorder
;
 from truth
 into concupiscence into burning
;
 from wisdom into the proprium into obst
inacy;
 from perception into shame
 into [
its
 final
 form
].


**¶8:** Yet
 these four faculties, when spiritual
 nourishment —
 the good
 and
 truth
 that
 flow
 in
 from the Divine through
 heaven
 — enters the natural man, are gathered
 in
ward and purified and cle
ansed and established in their living form
, which
 is the regenerated person. They receive
 the Divine Truth into
 the understanding —
 the illumin
ation
 that recon
stitutes the
 mind from
 within
 —
 and are restored to their original lik
eness to
 the Divine. They come forth from
 this
 process
 cle
ansed and holy, and
 attain the celest
ial peace that
 was their first state:
 the rest
 from
 which all
 spiritual
 combat
 had
 displaced
 them,
 which
 is the peace of heaven
 itself
.

---


*A
 note on the structure
:
*
 The teaching
 maps
 four
 fac
ulties through
 three
 desc
ending
 stages
 of
 corruption
 each
, yiel
ding twelve spiritual
 diseases
 of
 the natural
 man
. This
 is
 a
 precise
 interior
 anatomy
.
 The passage
 then
 rever
ses the entire
 cascade
 through
 a
 single
 principle
:
 the reception
 of spiritual nourishment — good
 con
jo
ined with truth — which
 recon
stitutes the "
new
 man."
 The correspondence
 of
 "
soul
 food" to
 the infl
ux of good
 and truth through
 regener
ation is exact
. The "
first
 rest" corresponds
 to what
 Swedenborg calls the peace
 of the
 celestial kingdom —
 the original
 and
 final
 state of the will
 turned
 wholly
 toward the Divine.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The discharge of this pollution, that [the fir]e shall disgorge and place in the body, is [blo]od. The discharge of the blood is anger. The discharge of anger is the humours.
Also, the emissions that the waters discharge from them are lust. The discharge of lust is bitterness. The emission of bitterness is f[e]ver.
The emission that light shall disgorge is flesh. The emission of flesh is gloom. [The] emission of gloom is obstinacy.
The emissions that the tree shall disgorge, they are the voices of the winds of shame. The emission of winds of shame [is grief. The emission of grief is the tear.]
The emission of the [tear] is the [completion] of these twelve emissions.

[But] these four elements shall [be purified. And] what are gathered in are [f]ound by the management of this soul food [that] enters the body. When they enter the body, they are cleansed and purified and established [i]n their living image, which is the new man. They shall live [again] and receive the Light Mind and be purified in their image; and they come forth, being cleansed and holy. They attain their first rest.

The four elements [are what is] purified. From the beginning they are holy ones, living ones, and enlighteners. However, when they undertood [ ... ] in that first struggle, the waste was [mixed] in with them, and the Darkness of the enemy was mixed with them. And when they were come into the body, stripping off these polluted garments, they set them in the flesh. Their pollutions, which they have stripped off, shall be displayed in a [ ... ] and become a danger to the body.
